subject: Film & Cinema
title: Rewriting and the Art of the Draft
description: A micro-lesson that makes Rewriting and the Art of the Draft usable.

hook.text: The first draft of Good Will Hunting was a spy thriller. Rewrites made it a character study.

buildup.text: Professional screenwriters often go through ten or more drafts before a film is greenlit.

discovery.text: Rewriting is where the real writing happens — first drafts discover, rewrites refine.

twist.text: Studios often hire different writers for different drafts, and credit battles get ugly.

climax.text: The finished script is rarely one person's vision — it's a palimpsest of many hands.

punchline.text: Writing is rewriting. Always has been.

quiz.question: Why do professional screenplays go through many drafts?
options: First drafts discover ideas, rewrites refine them
